summary: Moving turn_4 to Triton is worth one more run, but only as the dead-work-removal run on master's base, with the motivation's numbers corrected. The persistent grid (part 2) should not ride in this run until experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn harvests. Run the companion control (parts 1 and 3 only) now; hold the parent until the persistent-grid result, then rebuild it on that branch or retire it.
justification: Triton has never beaten Marlin at turn_4: stage 2 2100-2158 us, stage 3 2275-2318, packed-dequant-turn4 (ce3cc1a22a244ec7) 2149.0 sliding / 2306.1 full vs master Marlin 2148.2 / 2115.3 (c4d14d62f11e4aaf). That run's 1.052 headline is mostly first_turn on a stale base (no parallel align, no sorted silu). Master's _experts_triton already aligns over LOCAL_EXPERTS=32, so capacity at T=3012 is ~28.3K slots / ~221 tiles, not 444; ~165 remote -1 tiles remain (~10.5K early-return w13 CTAs, ~5K w2 CTAs zero-storing ~170 MB, ~35-40 us HBM). Realistic saving 50-120 us, putting Triton turn_4 at ~2.03-2.25 ms vs Marlin 2.12-2.15, inside the ~7% run-to-run spread. Weakest links: the dead-work premise measured on 257-expert-align bases; part 2 is the change under test in the running persistent-grid check and would mask the turn_4 read via first_turn (weight 186 of 310).
confounders: stack-tonight-five-prefill (master): 32-expert align already on the Triton path; sorted silu-mul only on the Marlin path, so turn_4 also swaps silu implementation (~10-30 us).
experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn (landed): this undoes its turn_4 half; the intended A/B.
experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 (landed): owns the reused BLOCK_T 128 config; its turn_4 rows vary ~7%.
experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn (running): part 2 is identical; rebuild or drop part 2 depending on its result.
interference: As written a single run is ambiguous both ways. Dispatch the control (parts 1 and 3, master's non-persistent grid) now; hold the parent until experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn harvests; if that gains, rebuild the parent on its branch adding only parts 1 and 3; if not, retire the parent and keep the control.
rules_flags: With local-only align, w2 never writes remote slots: fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum must mask them via slot_expert_ids; keep a NaN-poison prepare() check.
Shape gate on x.shape[0] only; local_start on device; OK.
Prepare checks at T=3012 and 16384 untimed; any PROGS_PER_SM decision from compiled metadata, not timing judge inputs.

companions.change: Built on master (a81d19c). Implement only parts (1) and (3) of the parent. (1) In _experts, send 1024 < T <= 4096 to _experts_triton (set MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS = 1024, with a comment); T <= 1024 keeps _experts_marlin. (3) In _experts_triton, when state['align_par_ok'] is set, replace moe_align_block_size(local_ids, cfg['BLOCK_T'], LOCAL_EXPERTS) with _align_parallel(local_ids, 0, LOCAL_EXPERTS, cfg['BLOCK_T']), which already exists on master for the Marlin path. Extend _align_par_setup's self-check to cover block 128 and 256 at T=3012 and 16384 (per-expert route sets vs moe_align_block_size). Because no -1 tiles remain, pass zero_nonlocal=False to the w2 call on this path. Add a prepare() NaN-poison check: fill cache3 with NaN, run the finalize, and assert a finite output. Run _check_experts_e2e at T=3012 as well as 8192 (rel L2 <= 2e-2, worst row <= 5x). Any failure sets MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS back to 4096 for the run and logs '[turn4-triton] OFF: <reason>'. Otherwise log 'ON'. _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel's grid stays as on master (no persistent loop). Everything else is unchanged.
